title: Beast movements v2
description: The `beast_movements` block: creatures whose species declares a movement class other than nester, and the circuits they walk. Groups share the shape of nomads.groups deliberately, so an encounter index or a time mover reads both with one code path. Structural envelope only; movement-class authoring is validated by Sim/tests/test_creature_movement.py and the irruption trigger by Sim/tests/test_beast_movements.py. Version 2 gave irruptions a condition in time: under version 1 every irruptive group marched in every year, so the block was a fixed roster of swarms a consumer could cache against the world's identity. It is now a function of the year on `world_clock` and changes from year to year.

stranded.description: Groups whose circuit could not be built. Reported and kept with their start camp rather than dropped, so a quiet world is distinguishable from a broken pass.

solitary.description: Irruptive groups in the solitary phase this year: sparse, holding their start camp, and not marching. A different fact from `stranded`, which is a route that could not be built. `routed + stranded + solitary` accounts for every group.

year.description: The absolute year the block was built for, from `world_clock.day`, or the world's founding year when it carries no clock yet.

year_forage_factor.description: This year's forage against an ordinary year's: one draw for the whole world, keyed on the genesis seed and the absolute year so a monthly tick cannot re-roll it. Below one is a lean year and more swarms march.

host_uid.description: For followers: the group whose circuit this one derives from. A nomad band or another creature group -- a follower does not search, it derives.

route_status.description: `routed` walks a circuit. `stranded` could not build one -- no reachable ground to move to. `solitary` is irruptive-only and is a normal state rather than a failure: a swarm that is not swarming this year, holding one base camp so the encounter index can still place it.
